title: Regional burn rate and unit economics grid — private VPC sizing
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet is a compact, region-aware capacity planner that ties GPU node BOM numbers to a simple token-cost / burn-rate model for Private/VPC customers. Intended for SRE + Solutions Eng pre-sales sizing and initial procurement guidance. Goal: produce per-region suggested node counts, spare pool, and 36-month amortized unit economics for planning conversations.

High-level approach (summary):
- Capture customer workload profiles: concurrency lanes, p50/p95 seq length, tokens/sec per request, steady vs. burst.
- Map workload to effective GPU throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) by model/quantization profile.
- Apply utilization target (e.g., 60% steady; 85% peak allowed for transient bursts) to compute required active nodes.
- Add operational buffers: spare pool, maintenance rotation, regional DR reserve.
- Convert nodes into BOM: chassis, GPU SKU, NICs, PSUs, racks, power budget.
- Amortize CapEx over X months and add OpEx (power, GCRs) for per-token and per-hour unit economics.

Assumptions (editable inputs):
- Target SLO: p95 latency budget 350ms for text generation workloads (affects batch sizing).
- Utilization baseline: steady_util = 0.60, burst_target = 0.85.
- Average request tokens: avg_tokens = 150; p95_tokens = 600
- Concurrency: concurrent_lanes = 40 (customer lane requests at steady)
- Model: opensource-70b-8bit -> throughput = baseline 350 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv (quantized runtime estimate)
- GPU SKUs considered: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, GH200-256GB (prices vary by procurement window)
- Node config templates: 8x A100 (dense), 4x H100 (large) — example BOMs below.

Quick input table (example):
Inputs | Region | Concurrency | avg_tokens | seq_p95 | steady_util | node_type | target_latency_ms
Sample | eu-west-1 | 40 | 150 | 600 | 0.60 | 8x-A100 | 350

Throughput math (cells/formula notes):
- tokens_per_sec_needed = concurrent_lanes * (avg_tokens / avg_latency_seconds)
  - avg_latency_seconds approximated from model throughput and batching. For conservative estimate use 0.6s per request => tokens_per_sec_needed = 40 * (150 / 0.6) = 10000 tokens/sec
- effective_gpu_throughput = 350 tokens/sec per GPU (runtime measurement for model/quantization)
- gpus_required_active = ceil(tokens_per_sec_needed / effective_gpu_throughput) => ceil(10000 / 350) = 29 gpus active
- nodes_required_active = ceil(gpus_required_active / gpus_per_node) => for 8x-A100 node => ceil(29/8) = 4 nodes active

Operational buffers (policy knobs):
- spare_pool_pct = 0.10 (10% of active nodes) => spare_nodes = ceil(4 * 0.10) = 1 node
- maintenance_rotation = 1 node per 48 nodes annually (rounded) -> small fleets may hold 1 extra for rotation
- DR reserve (optional) = 1 node per region for critical customers
- burst_headroom_policy: allow transient headroom up to burst_target - steady_util (0.85 - 0.60 = 0.25) => multiply active nodes by (1 + 0.25) when sizing for peak SLA

Example node sizing variants (BOM quick grid):
Columns: node_template | gpus_per_node | unit_cost_capex (USD) | rack_u | nameplate_power_W | example_parts_notes
8x-A100-1RU | 8 | 240000 | 2 | 6400 | Mellanox 200G, dual-PSU, NVMe for KV cache
4x-H100-2U | 4 | 210000 | 4 | 5200 | OCP-style chassis, 2x 100G, cold-aisle prep
2x-GH200-4U | 2 | 280000 | 8 | 11000 | high-memory nodes for LLAMA-like large context workloads
(Prices are placeholders — procurement to replace with actual quote)

Amortization and unit economics (method):
- amort_months = 36 (configurable)
- monthly_capex_per_node = unit_cost_capex / amort_months
- power_cost_per_node_month = (nameplate_power_W * 24 * 30 / 1000) * power_price_per_kwh (e.g., 0.12 USD/kWh) * power_draw_efficiency_factor (e.g., 0.85)
- monthly_ops (cooling, rack, network) = add-on, e.g., 1,200 USD/month/node baseline
- total_monthly_cost_per_node = monthly_capex_per_node + power_cost_per_node_month + monthly_ops
- per_token_cost = total_monthly_cost_per_region / (estimated_tokens_per_month)
  - estimated_tokens_per_month = tokens_per_sec_needed * 3600 * 24 * 30 * sustained_fraction (sustained fraction = steady_util)

Worked example (using sample above):
- tokens_per_sec_needed = 10,000 (from earlier)
- estimated_tokens_per_month = 10,000 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 0.60 ≈ 15.55e9 tokens/month
- nodes_total = active_nodes (4) + spare (1) + rotation/DR (1) = 6 nodes (8x-A100) -> total gpus = 48
- unit_cost_capex = 240,000 USD/node -> monthly_capex_per_node = 6,667 USD
- nameplate_power_W = 6400 -> power/month ~= (6.4 kW * 24 * 30) = 4,608 kWh -> cost @0.12 = 553 USD (apply efficiency factor => 650 USD)
- monthly_ops = 1,200 USD -> total_monthly_cost_per_node ≈ 6,667 + 650 + 1,200 = 8,517 USD
- total_monthly_region_cost = 8,517 * 6 = 51,102 USD
- per_token_cost = 51,102 / 15.55e9 = 3.28e-6 USD/token (approx) -> ~0.00328 USD per 1k tokens

Sensitivity knobs to play with in pre-sales:
- swap to H100 nodes: fewer nodes -> reduces spare/ops overhead but higher per-unit capex and power; recompute throughput gains per GPU
- change steady_util target: increasing to 0.70 reduces nodes but risks latency SLOs during bursts
- quantization profile changes throughput dramatically: 8-bit vs 4-bit estimates should be measured via runtime harness (link below)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- collect updated list pricing/lead times from procurement for A100/H100/GH200 by region (EMEA vs US pricing differs ~20%).
- verify real-world tokens/sec per GPU for "opensource-70b-8bit" from bench cluster (PR #211 bench run: link above).
- add thermal headroom and PDU layout sketch to BOM (current nodes assume average PUE 1.25 — confirm with infra).
- add example for bursty chat traffic where p95 tokens spike to 2k — runs different autoscaling profile.

Attachments and quick refs:
- Link to bench harness runs: gitlab/redwood/private-deploy/benchmarks#70b-8bit-2025
- Existing detailed workbook (for migration): shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/private-vpc-rightsize-workbook-2026.json (see that for alternate calculation flows)

Short next steps for this doc (v0 -> v1):
1) Replace placeholder unit_costs with procurement quotes for US/EU/APAC.
2) Add sheet tabs: a) Inputs, b) RegionCalc, c) NodeBOM, d) AmortGrid, e) Notes.
3) Add toggles for amort_months, power_price_per_kwh, and sustained_fraction and surface the per-1k-token cost immediately.
4) Run 3 representative customer scenarios (small, mid, large) and add to appendix.

Contact / owners: Ava Martinez (owner), Marco Li (benchmarks), Priya Shah (solutions-eng lead on EMEA quotes)

Notes on formatting: this is intentionally a compact sheet-style doc. The final deliverable should be exported as a Google Sheet with named ranges for the key inputs so SEs can customise per-customer quickly.

End of working draft.

-- Ava (11/02/2025)
